option_relations.rationale: Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia is a distinct genetic disorder of lipid metabolism, not directly related to the specific discordance between direct and calculated LDL-C measurements caused by elevated Lp(a).

Elevated Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is known to cause discordance between direct and calculated LDL cholesterol measurements, as Lp(a) particles contain apoB and can be measured as LDL-C by some assays, leading to an overestimation of LDL-C by calculated methods when Lp(a) is high.

Familial combined hyperlipidemia is a different genetic disorder characterized by elevated cholesterol and triglycerides, which does not specifically explain the discordance between direct and calculated LDL-C measurements due to Lp(a).
Lipoprotein(a) Hyperlipoproteinemia is synonymous with Elevated lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), which is the core diagnosis in this context.
